messages:
lia: heads-up — I'm exploring tweaking the policy 'cost_inertia' to reduce oscillation when we flip between region-affinity and cost-tier choices.
paul: can you sketch the current behavior? I remember inertia was ~0.2 default.
jin: short note — the formula we use is: `score = latency_w * latency + cost_w * cost + inertia * previous_score` which means previous_score mixes scales.
lia: exactly. that mixing is what's creating sticky route choices for big tenants. ran a quick sim, saw route flip suppression for 10s then abrupt flip.
paul: oh right — previous_score wasn't normalized before combining. that explains why large-score routes won out.
srin: proposal: apply inertia to the delta not the absolute. i.e. `new = base + inertia * (previous - base)`. dampens change while staying on the same scale.
andre: ops POV: changing scoring math is risky unless we can gate per-org. also need to consider eval ordering (affinity vs cost).
lia: agreed. thinking of a per-tenant feature flag `policy.v2.cost_inertia_delta` default off. rollout to canary orgs first.
jin: small code snippet for the new calc: `base = normalize(latency, cost); new_score = base + inertia * (prev_score - base); clamp(new_score, 0, 1)` — also add epsilon tie-breaker.
paul: tie-breaker should prefer lower-cost route for background/non-latency-sensitive traffic. for interactive apps prefer lower-latency. need per-route tags or workload-class.
lia: note: current system applies cost adjustments after affinity, so affinity can be stomped. we should either change ordering or make affinity a hard constraint when delta_latency > X ms.
andre: operationally changing ordering will impact a lot of tenants. suggest we add a transitional mode that logs both paths for 48h before toggling.
lia: sim results I ran with `./policy-sim --policy=cost-inertia.json --topology=multi-region-burst --seed=42` show 30% reduction in flip-rate at 95p latency, but 4% higher cost in worst-case without clamp.
srin: sounds reasonable. add clamp and per-tenant max_cost_increase.
jin: tests we need: unit tests for normalization, property tests for monotonicity, and integration runs in sim harness across 1000 random seeds.
paul: metrics to watch during canary: `route_flip_rate`, `95p_latency`, `cost_per_req`, `route_hotness`, and `policy_eval_time`. also watch `tokens/sec` and evictions.
lia: deployment plan draft: 1) land RFC PR with math and API, 2) implement behind `policy.v2.cost_inertia_delta`, 3) run sim and unit tests, 4) canary to 3 orgs for 6h, 5) evaluate metrics and promote. will include revert playbook.
andre: ops-bot: schedule canary window and create runbook for rollback.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled to canary orgs at 1765440000 (ETA) — :robot_face:
lia: also need to include model_variant multiplier in cost calc (quantization and kernel improvements change $/token).
paul: good catch. cost model = base_compute_cost * model_variant_multiplier + infra_surcharge. that feeds into normalized cost.
srin: also suggest deterministic fallback: if scores tie within epsilon, prefer lower-cost route for background classes and lower-latency for interactive — avoids noisy flips.
jin: QA note: add synthetic workload that toggles 30% long-tail bursts every 2 minutes to validate stability.
lia: I'm opening the RFC PR now (placeholder link) with math, rollout checklist, simulation outputs, and dashboard queries. will post here when ready.
paul: :thumbsup: please also add a migration note for existing saved policies — we must preserve backward compat.
lia: yes, we'll keep v1 semantics unless the flag is enabled. we'll also add a migration script to convert legacy configs.
andre: thanks — once PR is up ops will review runbook.
lia: thanks all — filing follow-ups: sim tweaks, unit tests, dashboard panels, and RFC writeup.
